raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
- `--fp8-gemm-backend=deep_gemm` now runs `[32, 32]` block-FP8 linears with UE8M0 scales (DeepSeek-V4.1) on DeepGEMM on SM100, instead of falling back to Triton. DeepGEMM serves this recipe there with `sm100_fp8_fp4_gemm_1d1d`.
- SM100 DeepGEMM casts the fp32 block scales to UE8M0 itself, which is exact only for powers of two. Weight loading checks that every block32 weight scale is a power of two (as the Hopper BF16 path already does) and the linear keeps any other layer on Triton, so a checkpoint labeled `ue8m0` with other scales keeps working. Pre-quantized `(q, scale)` input stays on Triton on SM100, since nothing checks its scales.
- Block32 weights without `scale_fmt: ue8m0` stay on Triton on SM100. An explicit `deep_gemm` that still lands on Triton for a non-128 block layout now logs a warning.
- `test_warmup_memory` now also covers the block32 kernel type on Blackwell.
- Verified on B300 through the real linear layer: UE8M0 weights run on DeepGEMM and match the Triton path within BF16 rounding over 5 shapes; scales scaled off powers of two fall back to Triton with output identical to Triton; pre-quantized input runs on Triton. Layer latency (N=4096, K=7168) drops from 135 us to 23 us at M=1, and from 1011 us to 56 us at M=2048.

Behavior changes only for `--fp8-gemm-backend=deep_gemm` on SM100; `auto`, the other backends, and SM90 are unchanged.

@@ -831,6 +831,15 @@ def process_weights_after_loading_block_quant(self, layer: Module) -> None:
 
         layer.weight.data = weight.data
         layer.weight_scale_inv.data = weight_scale.data
+        if use_deepgemm_runner and self.weight_block_size == [32, 32]:
+            from sglang.srt.layers import deep_gemm_wrapper
+
+            if deep_gemm_wrapper.DEEPGEMM_SCALE_UE8M0:
+                # UE8M0 DeepGEMM casts these fp32 scales in the kernel, which
+                # holds only for powers of two; the linear keeps others on Triton.
+                layer.weight_scale_inv.power_of_two = bool(
+                    (torch.frexp(weight_scale)[0] == 0.5).all().item()
+                )
         if hasattr(layer, "_block_fp8_bf16_weight"):
             layer._block_fp8_bf16_weight = None
             layer._derived_weight_cache_error = None

@@ -726,6 +730,12 @@ def dispatch_w8a8_block_fp8_linear(

     if weight_block_size is not None and weight_block_size[1] != 128:
+        if backend.is_deep_gemm():

+            )
         return partial(triton_w8a8_block_fp8_linear, act_scale_ue8m0=act_scale_ue8m0)
 
     # Handle explicit backend selection via --fp8-gemm-backend
@@ -1402,13 +1412,27 @@ def cutlass_w8a8_block_fp8_linear_with_fallback(
     return output.to(dtype=input_2d.dtype).view(*output_shape)
 
 
+def _ue8m0_deepgemm_skips_block32(
+    block_size: List[int],
+    weight_scale: torch.Tensor,
+    input_scale: Optional[torch.Tensor],
+) -> bool:
+    # UE8M0 DeepGEMM casts block32 fp32 scales itself: it takes only weights the
+    # load found power-of-two scaled, and no pre-quantized input, which nothing checks.
+    if list(block_size) != [32, 32] or not deep_gemm_wrapper.DEEPGEMM_SCALE_UE8M0:
+        return False
+    return input_scale is not None or not getattr(weight_scale, "power_of_two", False)
+

 ) -> bool:

     return list(block_size) == [128, 128] and n % 64 == 0 and k % 128 == 0

 ) -> torch.Tensor:

-        assert not deep_gemm_wrapper.DEEPGEMM_SCALE_UE8M0

+            list(block_size) == [32, 32] or not deep_gemm_wrapper.DEEPGEMM_SCALE_UE8M0
+        )
         assert input.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn
     output_dtype = torch.bfloat16 if input_scale is not None else input.dtype
 
     # TODO: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/6890#issuecomment-2943395737
